why: The first version of this treatment, and it is what the monotone case CANNOT catch: monotone is true of any increasing function, so a linear ramp passes it. Two measured defects. The parameter is a lerp between two reds the renderer tone-maps, and that transfer is compressive -- captured through the gallery, a linear parameter gives CIE L* 30.2 / 38.6 / 44.4 / 49.2 / 53.6 / 57.3 across six even steps of the fuse, so +8.4 in the first sixth against +3.7 in the last and the brightening reads DECELERATING, backwards for a fuse. And running the ramp over the full 0..1 leaves the fuse-warning window -- the distinct 'about to blow' cue -- about two just-noticeable differences, because the fuse has spent ~90% of the perceptual range before the window opens.
